page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-48 is an arm64-based virtual machine within the general-purpose compute tier. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs and 192 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server configuration includes zero GPUs and provides no integrated local disk storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring persistent storage and external connectivity to be provisioned separately.

Utilizing 64-bit Arm processor architecture with dedicated core allocation, the instance avoids thread contention and hypervisor throttling under sustained operational loads. The 192 GB memory pool offers adequate capacity for memory-resident worker pools, multi-stage data pipelines, and concurrent application threads operating across all 48 vCPUs.

From an operational perspective, the Arm-based architecture delivers favorable qualitative cost-to-core efficiency compared to traditional x86 allocations for workloads designed or recompiled for arm64. The primary tradeoffs involve the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning storage I/O throughput is governed by remote network disk performance, and the requirement for arm64 software compatibility. The platform is best fitted for containerized microservice clusters, multi-threaded CI/CD builds, web application serving, and distributed data processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-48 is an arm64 general-purpose instance equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 192 GB of system memory. Configured with a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU, it delivers consistent execution across multi-threaded applications without resource oversubscription. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, dedicated GPU hardware, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating network-attached storage solutions for all persistent file systems. Operating on 64-bit Arm architecture, the instance provides high compute density and qualitative operational cost efficiency for scale-out microservices, container clusters, continuous integration workflows, and data processing pipelines adapted for arm64 target environments.
